title: The Tabernacle
lead: The portable tent-sanctuary Israel built at Sinai so that God could "live in their midst" (Exodus 25:8). It traveled with Israel until Solomon's temple replaced it, and the New Testament takes up its language for Christ, who "pitched his tent among us" (John 1:14), and for the heavenly sanctuary (Hebrews 8–9; Revelation 21:3).

sections.b: After its building in Exodus 25–40, the tabernacle stands at the center of the camp (Numbers 2), and the Levites carry it on the march (Numbers 4). In the land it stands at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1; 1 Samuel 1–4), where the ark is lost to the Philistines. Psalm 78:60 says God abandoned the tent at Shiloh. Later texts place it at Nob and Gibeon (1 Samuel 21; 1 Chronicles 16:39; 2 Chronicles 1:3), while David pitches a new tent for the ark in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 6:17). God tells David he has always moved about in a tent (2 Samuel 7:6), and Solomon's temple finally takes its place (1 Kings 8:4). The New Testament reads it as a pattern of Christ (John 1:14), the heavenly sanctuary (Hebrews 8–9) and God's final dwelling with people (Revelation 21:3).
